hero.title: The Concept of Bodhisattvas
hero.description: A comprehensive study of the Mahayana Buddhist ideal—beings who delay their own Nirvana to alleviate the suffering of all sentient beings.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of the Bodhisattva ideal from Jataka stories to the philosophical heights of Mahayana Buddhism.

cards.details: Emergence of the Bodhisatta concept in Pali texts (Jataka tales) referring specifically to Siddhartha Gautama's previous births.
Formalization of the Bodhisattva ideal during the 4th Buddhist Council under Kanishka, distinguishing Mahayana from Theravada.
Flourishing of Bodhisattva iconography in Ajanta and Ellora, with figures like Avalokiteshvara becoming central to devotional practice.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks
mnemonics.description: Remember the primary Bodhisattvas with ease.

items.title: M.A.V.K
items.decryption: M (Future Buddha), A (Compassion), V (Power/Thunderbolt), K (Guardian of hell-beings).

items: Trap: Thinking Bodhisattvas are exclusive to Mahayana. Fact: The term existed in Theravada but refers only to the Buddha's previous lives, not a class of compassionate beings.
Trap: Confusing the Mudras (hand gestures) of Bodhisattvas with those of the Buddha.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Bodhi (Enlightenment) + Sattva (Being).
  • Compassion (Karuna) over personal salvation.
  • Universal salvation of all living beings.

Iconic Figures

  • Avalokiteshvara (Padmapani): Embodiment of mercy.
  • Maitreya: The future Buddha.
  • Vajrapani: Protector of the Buddha.
  • Evolutionary Mindmap:
    • Origins: Pali Canon (Jataka) → Focused on Siddhartha.
    • Shift: Mahayana expansion → Bodhisattva as a cosmic savior.
    • Practice: Paramitas (Perfections) required to attain Bodhisattvahood (Dana, Shila, Kshanti, etc.).
BodhisattvaAttributes
AvalokiteshvaraCompassion; Lotus-bearer (Padmapani)
MaitreyaFuture Buddha; Teaching pose
